text.p: The federal government has appointed a conciliator to help Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Co Ltd settle contract negotiations with its unionized workers, Hudson Bay Mining said in a release on Tuesday.

The conciliation officer will meet company representatives as well as the United Steelworkers of America, the Association of Flin Flon Trade Unions and the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers starting February 11, the company said.
Hudson Bay Mining, in Flin Flon in northern Manitoba, is controlled by Luxembourg-based Minorco SA.

The last contract with the zinc and copper operation's employees ended last October 1, the company said. The unions represent about 1,600 workers out of a total of 2,100 at operation's five mines and smelter.
Copper production from the smelter was 74,000 tonnes in 1995. Zinc production was 93,000 tonnes in 1995. Production figures for 1996 have not been released yet.
A company spokesman would not say what issues are standing in the way of an agreement.

The company and the unions have imposed a news blackout during labor talks, he said. The unions have not taken a strike vote and their old contract remains in force until a new one is reached, he added.
